previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis was admitted for nausea, nonbloody vomiting, and mild back pain, following a low-grade fever at home. Her creatinine was elevated to 1.2 on admission, consistent with prerenal acute kidney injury likely due to dehydration from vomiting. She received IV fluids, which resolved the renal dysfunction by discharge. Imaging showed cirrhotic liver and mild splenomegaly without acute findings. Blood and urine cultures were negative, ruling out infection. Her chronic abdominal and back pain remained stable, attributed to longstanding irritable bowel syndrome, cirrhosis, and musculoskeletal strain. She did not require narcotics at discharge and was advised to continue home medications and stay hydrated. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned.
